thesis: Hold QQQ, IWM, and NVDA. Cash is $0, so any buy is a sale of one of those lines. New pre-open items do not clear that bar. SoftBank's Masayoshi Son calls AI 50x the dot-com boom and says corrections could be the best opportunity; that is commentary with an empty summary and no US equity, and it supports keeping NVDA and QQQ rather than selling them. Anthropic's call for a coordinated halt plan if AI risks rise is the other side of the same tape, also with no listed target. The Apple-was-Buffett's-best and GOOGL-could-be-Abel's-claim headline is opinion, so I will not sell QQQ to add GOOGL or AAPL. Target-hijacks-Amazon, a gold-ETF question ahead of the June 16 Fed meeting, and automakers and retailers warning that a memory-chip shortage is hitting prices have empty summaries and no stated result; I will not invent TGT, GLD, or a memory name. Union Pacific's CEO rejecting a Trump stake in the railroad merger, the Northrop comparison, Assured Guaranty's insider sale, and the indie Semiconductor co-founder's $3.8M sale have no open in the tape. Yesterday's GME, AVGO, FLNC, and the other named ideas still have no open. No small-cap item against IWM. House PTRs are filings only, with no tickers.
